message.content:
Proof.
It is in NP.
A certificate is chosen vertices and edges.
We can verify that its total weight equals target k.
We now reduce from the standard decision problem known as Subset Sum here.
Given the input items, build one vertex per item and set each weight to its value.
The constructed graph has no edges at all, so every subgraph weight is the sum of chosen vertex values.
If a vertex subset has total weight k, then choosing exactly those vertices and no edges produces a subgraph of weight k.
Conversely, any subgraph of weight k selects some vertices, and those chosen item values sum exactly to k because no edges add weight at all.
Thus, because Subset Sum is NP Complete and the construction is polynomial, membership plus hardness proves this problem NP Complete for binary encoded weights of polynomial input length.
